records.title: Compute the topmost reporting candidates in one graph/topological pass
records.body:
🟡 Avoid pairwise whole-graph traversals when pruning consumer meters

For every ordered pair of collected consumer meters, this loop calls `reaches_any()`. Each call allocates a fresh visited set and may traverse the reachable graph, so pruning costs `O(k² × (V + E))` for `k` candidates, becoming cubic when the graph scales with the candidate count. Parallel feeds through silent meters are precisely what can cause both an ancestor and descendant meter to be collected here.

#### Impact
Formula generation can become disproportionately slow on valid meter-heavy or parallel-feed topologies, increasing CPU and setup/reconfiguration latency. This also reintroduces the repeated-graph-walk pattern that earlier optimization work in this repository removed.

#### Related locations

- https://github.com/frequenz-floss/frequenz-microgrid-component-graph-rs/blob/ca0e0cc5baef9f3019394eca82912caf1c4247d9/src/graph/retrieval.rs#L231-L257: every `reaches_any()` call creates a visited set and traverses reachable nodes.

#### Suggested fix
Compute the topmost reporting candidates in one graph/topological pass, or cache reachability per candidate instead of restarting traversal for every pair.

#### Suggested tests
Add a benchmark or instrumented traversal-count test with many candidates connected through silent parallel feeds, while retaining the existing shared-descendant case to lock de-duplication semantics.

---

🟡 Medium Severity: probably best to fix before merging because valid larger graphs can incur a substantial formula-generation regression.

_Originally posted by @llucax in https://github.com/frequenz-floss/frequenz-microgrid-component-graph-rs/pull/44#discussion_r3645358395_

records.title: Job Dependency Graph with DAG Execution
records.body:
## Overview
Implement job dependencies so that jobs can specify prerequisites and execute in correct order automatically.

## Problem
Complex workflows require manual orchestration. Users can't express "run job B only after job A succeeds" natively.

## Proposed Solution
- Define dependencies in job config: `depends_on: [job_id, job_id]`
- Build dependency DAG at submission time
- Detect cycles and reject invalid graphs
- Execute jobs in topological order
- Propagate failures: skip dependents if prerequisite fails
- Visual DAG editor in dashboard

## User Stories
- As a user, I want to chain jobs: build → test → deploy
- As a user, I want job B to auto-start when job A completes

## Labels
enhancement, needs-design

---

## Design Specification

### Current State Analysis

**Already Implemented:**

The codebase already has a robust foundation for job dependencies:

1. **Job Model** (`src/jobs.ts`):
   - `dependsOn: string[]` - array of job names this job depends on
   - `runOnDependencyFailure: boolean` - run even if dependencies failed
   - Validation for self-dependencies
   - Parsing from frontmatter with JSON array or comma-separated formats

2. **Workflow Execution** (`src/workflow.ts`):
   - `detectCircularDependencies()` - DFS-based cycle detection returning all cycle paths
   - `validateDependencies()` - validates all dependencies exist
   - `getReadyJobs()` - returns jobs whose dependencies are satisfied
   - `getExecutionOrder()` - topological sort using Kahn's algorithm
   - Dependency-aware execution with retry cascade support

3. **Workflow State** (`src/workflow-state.ts`, `src/workflow/state-manager.ts`):
   - In-memory and persistent state management
   - Job states: pending, running, success, failure, skipped, retrying
   - Automatic state transitions based on dependency completion

4. **Visualization** (`src/ui/services/workflow-visualization.ts`):
   - Builds workflow graph (nodes + edges)
   - Formats as Mermaid diagrams with status styling
   - Shows execution order

5. **Test Coverage** (`src/__tests__/workflow-dependencies.test.ts`):
   - Sequential chains, parallel branches, failure propagation
   - Cycle detection, missing dependency validation
   - 378 lines of comprehensive tests

### What Needs to Be Built

#### 1. Dashboard Dependency Graph Visualization

**Current Gap:** No interactive visualization in the web dashboard.

**Proposed Solution:**

```
src/ui/components/
├── DependencyGraph.tsx    # Interactive DAG visualization
├── GraphControls.tsx     # Zoom, pan, filter controls
└── JobNode.tsx           # Individual job node component
```

**Features:**
- Interactive SVG/Canvas-based DAG rendering
- Node colors by status (pending, running, success, failure, skipped)
- Click-to-select nodes showing job details
- Real-time status updates via WebSocket
- Zoom/pan controls for large graphs
- Filter by status or tag
- Minimap for navigation

**Implementation Options:**

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|--------|------|------|
| D3.js | Flexible, powerful, existing ecosystem | Steep learning curve |
| React Flow | Built for DAGs, interactive | Larger bundle |
| Custom SVG | Lightweight, full control | More code to maintain |
| Mermaid (existing) | Already implemented | Limited interactivity |

**Recommendation:** React Flow for rich interactivity with minimal code.

#### 2. Job Configuration UX

**Current Gap:** Dependencies specified via raw YAML in job files.

**Proposed Solution:**

Add dependency management to the job template marketplace:

```yaml
---
# Job template with dependency selection
schedule: "0 10 * * *"
prompt: "Run integration tests"
dependsOn: []           # UI: Multi-select dropdown of available jobs
runOnDependencyFailure: false  # UI: Checkbox
---
```

**Dashboard Enhancements:**
- Dependency dropdown populated from existing jobs
- Visual dependency builder (drag-and-drop)
- Real-time cycle detection feedback
- Dependency validation warnings

#### 3. Enhanced API Endpoints

**Current Gap:** No API for dependency graph operations.

**New Endpoints:**

```typescript
// GET /api/workflow/graph
interface WorkflowGraphResponse {
  nodes: JobNode[];
  edges: DependencyEdge[];
  executionOrder: string[];
  cycles: string[][];
  warnings: string[];
}

// POST /api/workflow/validate
interface ValidateRequest {
  jobs: Job[];
}
interface ValidateResponse {
  valid: boolean;
  cycles: string[][];
  missingDependencies: { jobName: string; missing: string[] }[];
  warnings: string[];
}

// POST /api/workflow/execute
interface ExecuteRequest {
  workflowId?: string;
  trigger: "manual" | "webhook" | "schedule";
  dryRun?: boolean;
}
interface ExecuteResponse {
  workflowId: string;
  executionPlan: { job: string; dependsOn: string[]; parallelGroup: number }[];
}
```

records.title: Call graph characteristics: descriptive layers on a member-centric graph
records.body:
## Summary

Keep the call graph **member-centric** (nodes are member identities; edges are call evidence). Generalize the **shape** by making **characteristics** first-class — the same separation AnnotatedSource uses for facts vs text — so viewers can enable/filter rich description without changing identity or baking everything into labels.

This is the descriptive half of multi-package / multi-provider / package-web demos. It complements mode split (#4133) and cross-library resolution (#3632); it does not replace them.

## Motivation

Member-centric CG is correct for call evidence. Demos still need:

- package/library/type **context** without making those the primary node id
- **arc** meaning (calls vs extends vs integration vs references)
- perf/risk **signals** (partially present via `--fields` on nodes)
- optional **Findings** overlays
- lean defaults; dense detail only when requested

Today:

| Piece | State |
| ----- | ----- |
| Topology | Strong (`CallGraphProjection` nodes/edges/focus) |
| Node scale + body signals | Partial (`--fields` → fanout/alloc/throw/… in labels) |
| Edge labels | Thin (`GraphEdge.Label` ≈ loop only) |
| Integration / package-web on arcs | Missing (extensions stay a table; integrations a separate section) |
| Characteristic catalog separate from display strings | Missing (most description is formatted into node text) |

AnnotatedSourceDocument lesson: **carrier + facts + targets + viewer filter**, not a fatter string. Call graph needs the graph-shaped analogue: **topology + characteristics + subject binding + viewer filter**.

## Design intent

### Substrate (unchanged)

- Node identity: member (structural / `MemberRef`-class evidence).
- Edge identity: call evidence (kind, loop, caller/callee).
- Focus: one seed member in seed-centric mode (#4133); ad hoc mode may have multiple seeds or none privileged.
- Package and type are **scope, group, aggregation lens, or characteristics** — not a second IR that abandons members.

### Characteristic plane (new)

```text
CallGraphDocument (conceptual)
  nodes[], edges[]                 // topology + identity
  characteristics[]                // first-class descriptors
  // each characteristic: id, kind/layer, subject (node|edge|path), payload
  // viewer selects layers / fields; sinks (MD table, tree, Mermaid) project
```

**Layers (illustrative catalog — not a frozen enum):**

| Layer | Typical subject | Examples |
| ----- | --------------- | -------- |
| Scale | node | fanin, fanout, depth |
| Body cost/risk | node | alloc, copy, unsafe, throw, catch (today’s signals) |
| Relationship kind | edge | calls, virtual/interface dispatch, newobj |
| Call facts | edge | loop, external, external→resolved (#3632) |
| Boundary | node and/or edge | package, library, group id |
| Integration | edge and/or node | `Integration: AI`, `Integration: Aspire` |
| API spelling on relationship graphs | edge | `AddOpenAI`, `AsIChatClient` (package web / adapters) |
| Findings | node/edge opt-in | cycle finding id, perf opportunity id |

Progressive disclosure: default graph stays readable (identity + minimal scale). Characteristics never appear unless selected (same spirit as signals-not-in-default-view in `docs/design/graph-signal-annotations.md`).

### Mermaid

Edge labels are supported: `A -->|label| B`. Node text and edge labels are **projections** of selected characteristics, not the store. GitHub and Markout can render them; contract is structured characteristics first.

### Relationship to other graphs

Same **envelope** (nodes, edges, groups, focus, characteristics) can host:

- **Call graph** — member nodes, call edges (this issue’s home).
- **Package web** — e.g. hub type → packages with `extends` + method + integration on arcs (may be a sibling producer; still member- or type-keyed evidence underneath where applicable).
- **Type rollup** — aggregation lens over member edges, not a replacement identity model.

Do not force `depends` or touchpoints (#3630) to become call graphs; they may share presentation machinery.

## Non-goals

- Replacing member identity with package- or type-only nodes as the sole model.
- Putting every body Finding on every node by default.
- Faking multi-provider edges from `Aspire.Hosting.OpenAI.AddOpenAI` (no refs to MEAI/Azure.AI/Bedrock).
- Blocking seed-centric demos until the full catalog lands.

## Relationship to existing work

| Issue / doc | Role |
| ----------- | ---- |
| #4133 | Seed-centric vs ad hoc **modes** (how the graph is built) |
| #3632 | Resolve externals into bodies (evidence quality for characteristics like external→resolved) |
| #3292 | Depth / multi-lib UX / command-vs-section (surface for selectors) |
| #3469 | Relationship arc vocabulary (call-site modality vs propagated facts) — align catalogs |
| `docs/design/graph-signal-annotations.md` | Existing **node** signal projection via `--fields` — fold into characteristic model, don’t fork |
| AnnotatedSource facts/targets | Separation-of-concerns

records.title: feat(runtime): propagate renegotiated endpoints through the dependency graph
records.body:
## Problem

Issue #869 allocates runtime and service endpoints before launch, but a changed endpoint is only useful when every consumer is rematerialised from the resolved value. Services can otherwise start with stale environment values, command arguments, generated files, health targets, routes or UI links.

A simple service-order restart is insufficient: the runtime must know which consumers depend on which endpoint and apply the new generation consistently.

## Goal

Build a dependency-aware reconfiguration and cutover contract for endpoint changes. A renegotiated endpoint must propagate to all affected consumers before they are considered part of the committed runtime generation.

## Dependencies

- #810 — canonical endpoint model and selectors
- #869 — startup-wide endpoint allocation and renegotiation
- #876 — authoritative runtime generation

## Scope boundary

#869 owns endpoint discovery, conflict detection, allocation and reservation. This issue owns impact analysis, rematerialisation, restart ordering and proof that consumers use the new resolved values.

## Required behaviour

- Build a directed dependency graph from manifest dependencies plus endpoint selector references.
- Record which materialised artefacts consume each resolved endpoint.
- Calculate the minimal impacted service set when an endpoint changes.
- Regenerate environment/global environment, commands, config files, URLs, routes and health checks from one allocation revision.
- Restart or reload affected consumers in topological order according to explicit service capability.
- Keep old and new revisions distinguishable during cutover.
- Fail before mutation for dependency cycles that cannot be ordered safely.
- Roll back through the startup transaction when rematerialisation/restart fails.
- Publish configuration/allocation digests for diagnosis without exposing values or secrets.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Endpoint selectors, not copied numeric ports, drive dependent configuration.
- [ ] A provider port change identifies every direct and transitive consumer.
- [ ] Only the minimal affected set is rematerialised/restarted.
- [ ] Consumers start after providers and read the same allocation revision.
- [ ] Generated files, commands, env, health checks, routes and API links all use the new value.
- [ ] Reload-capable services may reload; others restart through normal lifecycle policy.
- [ ] Cycles and unsupported dynamic changes fail with actionable evidence.
- [ ] A partial cutover is rolled back safely.
- [ ] Tests cover direct, transitive, fan-out and cyclic dependencies plus failure during cutover.
- [ ] Verification proves no stale proposed/pre-change port remains in effective configuration.

## OpenSpec binding

- `.governance/specs/SPEC-002-core-standalone-runtime.md`
- Proposed `AC-4BK`: dependency-aware endpoint rematerialisation and generation-consistent cutover.

## Backlog classification

- Area: core runtime / endpoint propagation
- Type: reliability hardening
- Priority: P0

## Dependency refinement

This issue also depends on #877. The dependency cutover must run inside the durable startup/recovery transaction so a failed rematerialisation or restart has generation-scoped compensating actions rather than an independent rollback mechanism.

records.title: feat(code): derive import, dependency, inheritance, and call relations
records.body:
## Outcome

Add a provenance-bearing code relationship graph that helps agents navigate architecture and impact without treating inferred edges as canonical source.

## Scope

- model file/module imports, package dependencies, inheritance/implementation, symbol calls, containment, and reference edges
- preserve repository/revision, source span, parser version, confidence, and edge origin
- distinguish syntactic direct edges from resolved, inferred, dynamic, or unresolved relations
- expose bounded neighborhood, callers/callees, dependency, and impact queries through code APIs and graph views
- update relations incrementally when files or parser versions change
- enforce project/ACL scope before traversal or serialization

## Acceptance criteria

- every edge is traceable to canonical source or explicitly marked inference
- unresolved dynamic behavior is never presented as certainty
- graph traversal is paginated, depth-bounded, cycle-safe, and resource-bounded
- changed or deleted code invalidates affected edges deterministically
- fixtures cover cycles, interfaces, aliases, dynamic calls, generated code, and cross-repository dependencies

## Dependencies

- depends on symbol indexing in #2071

records.title: Recompile only what changed: a reverse dependency walk, structural sharing, and a differential test
records.body:
## Summary

Add `compile_incremental`: given the previous snapshot and a `ChangeSet`, mark the affected units dirty by
walking the fixed four-level dependency graph, rebuild only those, and share every unchanged subtree by
`Arc` clone. Prove it correct with a differential property test asserting the incremental result is
semantically identical to a full compile of the same bundle, and gate it with the two numbers that matter:
a one-route change against a live 100,000-route table, and the allocation count of everything except the
route table.

## Context

Incremental compile is architectural, not an optimisation. It is what dictates that `Snapshot` is a tree of
`Arc`s and that resources carry content hashes, so retrofitting it means rewriting the snapshot type. It is
also the single most defensible differentiator in this milestone: Kong shipped full-configuration broadcast
for years, found it to be the binding constraint on propagation delay, memory and CPU, then fixed it in
Gateway 3.10 and, per Kong's own documentation, made incremental configuration sync available only in
Kong Enterprise and not supported in Kong OSS. Traefik still recomputes the entire merged configuration per
provider event with a full structural compare and several deep copies. Shipping incremental sync in the open
source core is a direct, defensible advantage, and this issue is where it becomes true.

The dependency graph is fixed, shallow and known at compile time:

```
Certificate  -> Listener            (through the certificate references)
Upstream     -> ClusterSnapshot     (endpoints and transport)
Listener     -> Route               (hostname intersection and attachment)
Route        -> RouteTable          (the compiled table)
Role         -> nothing in the data plane
```

Three properties of that graph do the work:

1. **An endpoint change dirties no route.** `ClusterId` is keyed on the upstream's resource identity, so
   changing an upstream's endpoints, weights or health rebuilds one `ClusterSnapshot` and leaves every route
   that references it byte-identical. This is what makes an EndpointSlice storm cost O(changed endpoints)
   rather than O(routes). It is also the answer to the fan-out worry: an upstream referenced by every route
   is marked dirty once, at the upstream, and never propagated to the routes.
2. **A role change compiles nothing.** RBAC is evaluated by the admin API, not by the data plane, so a role
   edit publishes a snapshot in which every field is `Arc::ptr_eq` with the previous one. The publish still
   happens, because the bundle version must advance and the audit trail must record it.
3. **A certificate change touches listeners, never routes.** The TLS material is rebuilt and the route table
   is shared verbatim.

For the route table itself, the router already provides the incremental machinery:
`RouteTableBuilder::rebuild_from(previous, generation)` reuses by `Arc` clone every group whose content hash,
chain successor, name set and pattern list are unchanged, and it is documented to produce a table
byte-identical to a full build. Our job is to feed it and to decide when it is safe to call, not to
re-implement group reuse.

One honest limitation, stated here so nobody chases a number that is not available: `add_http_route` takes a
route by value, so an incremental compile still re-admits every route, which is an O(n) pass with a small
constant. The trie building, the group arenas and the literal blobs are what `rebuild_from` avoids, and they
are the expensive part. Making admission itself incremental requires a router-side API that accepts a
previously admitted route set, which is a router change and is out of scope here. The benchmark therefore
reports the re-admission cost separately rather than hiding it inside a headline number.

## Files

| Path | Action | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/irontraffic-config-compile/src/dirty.rs` | create | `DirtyKind`, `DirtySet`, `propagate` |
| `crates/irontraffic-config-compile/src/incremental.rs` | create | `compile_incremental`, `IncrementalStats` |
| `crates/irontraffic-config-compile/src/lib.rs` | modify | declare and re-export the two modules |
| `crates/irontraffic-config-compile/tests/incremental.rs` | create | the differential test and the sharing assertions |
| `crates/irontraffic-config-compile/fuzz/Cargo.toml` | create or modify | the fuzz crate for this crate |
| `crates/irontraffic-config-compile/fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_incremental.rs` | create | the incremental-equals-full fuzz target |
| `crates/irontraffic-config-compile/benches/lower.rs` | modify | incremental scaling and the allocation gate |

Files not in this table MUST NOT be touched.

## Design

### The dirty set

```rust
/// What kind of work a change implies.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum DirtyKind {
    /// One cluster snapshot must be rebuilt.
    Cluster,
    /// One listener must be recompiled, which may mean a rebind.

records.title: ouroboros-db: [AK.5] Planning constraints in ci/db
records.body:
## Quick Summary | | | |---|---| | **Epic** | #268 — AK · Planning Domain (`ouroboros-db`) | | **Level of effort** | XS | | **Affected systems** | Database, CI, `ouroboros-db`, `.github` | | **Release** | 🟢 MVP (v1) | | **Milestone** | Planning MVP | | **Type** | Task | Planning invariants added to the `ci/db` constraint suite — acyclicity, push-state vocabulary, and month-range sanity. ## Design Reference [`docs/mockups/09-planning.html`](https://github.com/NobuData/ouroboros/blob/main/docs/mockups/09-planning.html) — the invariants under test are what the visible behaviour depends on: dependency-ordered push (`blocks OTA-3`), per-draft push states, and the gantt's month-ranged lanes. ## Problem Statement Three of this roadmap's guarantees are enforced in application code, and each has a database-observable failure mode worth catching in CI. **Acyclicity** is checked service-side (AL.4, #280) because detecting a cycle means walking a graph. But if that check has a bug, the damage lands in the database — and the symptom is not an error, it is a batch that can **never be pushed**, because AL.3 (#279) orders pushes by dependency and a cycle has no valid order. A recursive-CTE probe over stored rows catches that class of bug at build time rather than at push time. **Push-state transitions** decide whether resume works. A draft that reaches `pushed` and then somehow returns to `pending` would be pushed twice, creating the duplicate issue that decision N6 exists to prevent. **Month ranges** feed the gantt's geometry. A lane whose `end_month` precedes its `start_month` renders as a negative-width bar, and one with a single null of the pair renders as nothing at all — both are silent, and both look like a UI bug rather than bad data. ## Solution / Scope Extend the #24 `tests/constraints.sql` probes: - **Stored-cycle detection** — a recursive CTE over `ticket_dependencies` asserting no cycle exists in the seeded graph, and failing loudly when one is planted. - **Exactly-one-kind dependency references** — an endpoint with both or neither of its draft/ticket references set is rejected. - **Push-state vocabulary** — only `pending|pushed|failed` are storable. - **Epic range ordering** — `start_month` ≤ `end_month`, and the pair is **both-or-neither**. - **Tint and status vocabularies** — constrained to the mockup's sets. - **Unique batch-local keys** — `OTA-1` cannot repeat within a batch. Each probe names the invariant it protects, so a red build says *which* guarantee disappeared. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] Green against the AK.4 (#275) seeds. - [ ] **Red on a planted cycle** — spot-verified by inserting one. - [ ] **Red on a reversed month range** — spot-verified. - [ ] Red on a half-null date pair, a duplicate local key, and an out-of-vocabulary push state. - [ ] Failures name the invariant, not just the SQL error. - [ ] Runs inside the existing `ci/db` job with no meaningful runtime increase. ## Parallelism / Dependencies Needs AK.4 (#275) and #24 (migration CI check). Protects the assumptions AL.3 (#279) and AL.4 (#280) rely on. ## Technical Stack GitHub Actions, PostgreSQL 17, SQL (recursive CTEs). ## Relationships - Parent epic: #268 - Depends on: #275, #24 - Protects: #279 (dependency-ordered push), #280 (service-side acyclicity) ## Diagram ```mermaid flowchart LR MIG["flyway migrate (planning schema)"] --> C["constraints.sql + AK probes"] C --> P1["recursive CTE: no stored dependency cycle
(a cycle = a batch that can NEVER be pushed)"] C --> P2["exactly-one-kind endpoint refs"] C --> P3["push_state vocab — pushed cannot revert to pending
(a revert would push twice — the N6 duplicate)"] C --> P4["epic range: start ≤ end · both-or-neither
(reversed = negative-width bar; half-null = invisible lane)"] C --> P5["tint + status vocabs"] C --> P6["unique batch-local keys (OTA-1 once per batch)"] P1 & P2 & P3 & P4 & P5 & P6 --> V{"all invalid states rejected?"} V -->|yes| OK["✓ green"] V -->|no| BAD["✗ named invariant lost"] ``` --- Created by **Ouroboros**

records.title: July algorithms sprint
records.body:
## 🏃 Four-Week Intensive Algorithms Study Sprint — July 1–31

A structured daily study plan to prepare for the algorithms certification exam. Each week focuses on a core theme, with daily sessions designed to build depth progressively.

---

### Week 1 (July 1–7) — Foundations & Complexity
Build a solid base before diving into advanced topics.
- **Day 1:** Big-O notation, time & space complexity analysis
- **Day 2:** Arrays and strings — core operations and edge cases
- **Day 3:** Linked lists — singly, doubly, circular
- **Day 4:** Stacks and queues — implementations and use cases
- **Day 5:** Recursion fundamentals and call stack intuition
- **Day 6:** Practice set — mixed foundational problems
- **Day 7:** Review + weak-area reinforcement

---

### Week 2 (July 8–14) — Sorting, Searching & Hashing
Master the most commonly tested algorithm families.
- **Day 8:** Bubble, selection, insertion sort
- **Day 9:** Merge sort and quicksort (divide & conquer)
- **Day 10:** Binary search and its variations
- **Day 11:** Hash tables — collision handling, load factor
- **Day 12:** Two-pointer and sliding window patterns
- **Day 13:** Practice set — sorting and searching problems
- **Day 14:** Review + timed problem-solving drill

---

### Week 3 (July 15–21) — Trees, Graphs & Dynamic Programming
Tackle the most conceptually demanding topics.
- **Day 15:** Binary trees — traversals (inorder, preorder, postorder)
- **Day 16:** Binary search trees — insert, delete, search
- **Day 17:** Heaps and priority queues
- **Day 18:** Graph representations — adjacency list vs matrix
- **Day 19:** BFS and DFS — iterative and recursive
- **Day 20:** Dynamic programming — memoization and tabulation
- **Day 21:** Classic DP problems (knapsack, coin change, LCS)

---

### Week 4 (July 22–31) — Advanced Topics, Mock Exams & Review
Consolidate knowledge and simulate exam conditions.
- **Day 22:** Greedy algorithms and when to apply them
- **Day 23:** Backtracking — N-queens, permutations, subsets
- **Day 24:** Tries and advanced string algorithms
- **Day 25:** Shortest path algorithms (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford)
- **Day 26:** Union-Find / Disjoint Set Union
- **Day 27:** Full mock exam #1 (timed, closed notes)
- **Day 28:** Mock exam review — analyse mistakes and gaps
- **Day 29:** Targeted revision based on mock results
- **Day 30:** Full mock exam #2 (timed, closed notes)
- **Day 31:** Final review, confidence check, and exam prep wrap-up

---

### Daily Session Structure (suggested)
| Block | Duration | Activity |
|---|---|---|
| Warm-up | 15 min | Review previous day's notes |
| Core study | 45 min | New concept + worked examples |
| Practice | 45 min | 3–5 problems on the day's topic |
| Debrief | 15 min | Log what clicked, what didn't |

**Total: ~2 hours/day**

---

> Track daily progress in the comments. Flag blockers early so the plan can be adjusted. Good luck! 🚀

records.title: EPIC: real conversation, code, and heterogeneous-model consensus through MCP/OpenAI
records.body:
## Outcome

Laplace serves real multi-turn conversation, novel code generation with toolchain feedback, and one pooled answer from heterogeneous model testimony through MCP and the OpenAI-compatible endpoint—without a GPU requirement, external answer-writing LLM, runtime model ensemble, post-hoc judge, or tensor merge.

Product definition and measured audit: `docs/plan/REAL_CONVERSATION_AND_MODEL_CONSENSUS_FINISH_LINE.md`.

## What this means

A conversation is a witnessed session trajectory. A model is a source of exact checkpoint/circuit testimony. Multiple models do not each answer; their evidence joins the shared content-addressed substrate, consensus folds before inference, and one canonical CPU-native forward pass produces one response.

The model claim is not MergeKit-style arithmetic. The acceptance environment includes incompatible causal, encoder/embedding, reranker/MoE, and later multimodal checkpoints. Canonical entities, typed relations, tiers, circuit factors/trajectories, PostGIS geometry, source witnesses, and Glicko state are the common execution plane.

## Blocking delivery issues

- [ ] #920 — deployed MCP launcher and live JSON-RPC proof.
- [ ] #921 — one stateful dynamic-frontier forward pass shared by MCP/OpenAI.
- [ ] #922 — honest OpenAI roles/parameters/Responses/tools and a real code lane.
- [ ] #923 — source-scoped circuit comparison cube and cross-architecture correlation.
- [ ] #927 — one pooled heterogeneous-source forward pass with A/B/A+B ablation.
- [ ] #928 — deterministic source-scoped and pooled model export with provenance receipts.
- [ ] #929 — machine-readable seed capability manifest for every dataset/source.
- [ ] #755 — seeded product evaluation gate (reopened; election-only success is insufficient).

## Repository governance

- [ ] #926 — one documentation and agent-instruction authority hierarchy; no stale reports or agent memories as work authority.

## Existing owners incorporated into the finish line

- [ ] #350 — trajectory ordinal continuity performance/default.
- [ ] #354 — retire/consolidate rival traversal engines in implementation.
- [ ] #360 — session as a trajectory entity.
- [ ] #368, #369, #370 — model scorer, OODA fold, deep-layer replay.
- [ ] #756, #757 — typed question routing and both-direction/n-hop inference.
- [ ] #811 — every substrate question reachable as a typed operation.
- [ ] #894 — code-as-player generate/stage/compile-test/witness/fold loop.
- [ ] #8, #111, #112, #475, #476, #488 — external model round-trip and fidelity proof.

## Final acceptance demonstration

One automated script, starting from a declared seed profile and using no manual SQL, must:

1. initialize the deployed MCP and list/call the product tools;
2. hold a multi-turn conversation through MCP and HTTP, including correction, anaphora, topic return, and abstention;
3. show the same canonical trace semantics through streaming and non-streaming;
4. generate a new bounded code artifact, compile/test it, witness the outcome, and show the fold affects a subsequent decision;
5. ingest at least three incompatible local model sources;
6. answer `King → all model circuits`, compare one same-ordinal circuit across sources, and find/explain one cross-ordinal correlation;
7. query pooled model consensus once and return one answer—no N candidates or judge;
8. show A-only, B-only, and A+B scopes as diagnostic evidence/ablation, not answer selection;
9. export a source-scoped model and a pooled-consensus model deterministically;
10. load the export in the declared external runtime and pass held-out semantic probes.

## Non-success

The epic does not close for non-empty prose, template recall, one successful prompt, topic-only session state, accepted-but-ignored API fields, tensor/layer merging, MoE routing over original models, post-query voting, a GGUF that only exists on disk, or an election harness that defers HTTP generation.

## Evidence rule

Running behavior > executable code/tests > binding invariants > receipts > plans/issues. Closed child status cannot override an unmet behavioral checkbox.

records.title: Extension Dependencies and Provided Services
records.body:
## Problem Statement

Extension authors cannot build on top of other Extensions. Every Extension is an island: if two Extensions need the same expensive or stateful capability (a headless browser, a sandbox, a vector index, a telemetry pipeline), each must construct its own instance, and the duplicates silently diverge — the Agent writes a file in one sandbox and runs tests in another. Authors who want to layer functionality (a cost-guard on top of an OpenTelemetry Extension, screenshot tools on top of a shared browser) have no supported way to express "that Extension must be active in this Agent, before me, and I need typed access to what it publishes."

## Solution

Extensions gain two declarative fields:

- **Extension Dependencies** — an Extension declares other Extensions that must be active in the same Agent Definition. Dependencies are auto-included, deduplicated, and loaded dependency-first; the Agent author's `extensions` array stays a flat list of what they chose.
- **Provided Services** — an Extension deliberately publishes selected services from its Resource Layer as a typed contract. Dependents' Tool handlers and Hooks access those services with full type inference; everything not published stays private. One instance per Session, shared by all dependents.

The existing compile-time resource-coverage rule extends across dependency edges: using a service that is neither in your own Resource Layer nor in a declared dependency's Provided Services is a compile error, not a runtime defect.

## User Stories

1. As an Extension author, I want to declare Extension Dependencies, so that my Extension can rely on another Extension being active without asking users to wire it manually.
2. As an Extension author, I want to publish selected services from my Resource Layer as Provided Services, so that other Extensions can build on my functionality through a typed contract.
3. As an Extension author, I want services I do not publish to remain private, so that internal refactors never break dependents.
4. As an Extension author, I want my Tool handlers and Hooks to get typed access to my dependencies' Provided Services, so that I get inference, autocomplete, and jump-to-definition instead of runtime lookups.
5. As an Extension author, I want a compile error when a handler or Hook uses a service not covered by my Resource Layer or my dependencies' Provided Services, so that missing-service defects are impossible at runtime.
6. As an Extension author, I want to declare a dependency once and have its Provided Services available to every handler and Hook in my Extension, so that I never plumb context manually.
7. As an Extension author, I want to define a shared service contract as a Tag and accept alternative implementations as plain Layers via my configuration, so that the community can implement providers (search backends, crawlers) without those implementations being Extensions themselves.
8. As an Agent author, I want dependencies auto-included and deduplicated, so that declaring `screenshot()` and `scraper()` gives me exactly one shared browser Extension.
9. As an Agent author, I want a compile failure when the same Extension name is reached twice with different values, so that conflicting configurations are never silently resolved.
10. As an Agent author, I want a compile failure on dependency cycles, reported with the cycle path, so that a broken Extension graph is caught before any Session starts.
11. As an Agent author, I want Hooks and Instructions to compose in a deterministic dependency-first order that is stable with respect to my declaration order, so that behavior does not change between runs.
12. As an Agent author, I want exactly one instance of each Provided Service per Session, so that expensive resources are not duplicated and cross-Tool state stays consistent.
13. As an Agent author, I want Provided Services torn down in reverse dependency order at Session end, so that dependents never outlive what they depend on.
14. As an SDK library user, I want the dependency graph to work identically when mitome is embedded in my application, so that there is one authoring model for CLI and library usage.
15. As an ecosystem author, I want to ship a curated bundle as a plain function returning a list of Extensions with a typed options surface, so that I can offer presets without any framework merge machinery.
16. As a maintainer, I want all graph failures aggregated into the existing Agent Definition compile error with deterministic ordering, so that authors see every problem in one pass.

## Implementation Decisions

- The Extension value gains optional `dependencies` (a list of Extension values) and `provides` (a list of service Tags selecting which outputs of the single Resource Layer are public). There is deliberately no second Layer: Provided Services are built by the same Layer that builds private Resources, so publishing something built on private internals is ordinary Effect composition.
